Hey all,

I'm pretty excited that somebody has already set up a community here to discuss craft cocktails. I've found in my experience bartending that people can be easily intimidated by the overwhelming world of cocktails, and I've made it my mission to lower the bar for inexperienced cocktail drinkers. Cocktails shouldn't be pretentious or exclusive, they should be created in order to be enjoyed by everyone. A lot of guests are not as immersed in the current craft movement and can be easily put off by the mustachioed bartender listing off obscure ingredients in a variety of languages or boasting of his house-made syrups, shrubs, or bitters. Let's not be them! Don't make it too complicated. Just enjoy the drink!

At the same time, it's great to be able to geek out with fellow enthusiasts.

So as an introduction I'd like to share my favorite simple cocktail: The Japanese cocktail

This drink is over a hundred years old, and is incredibly easy to make.

  • 2 oz. Brandy (traditionally Cognac, but also great with Armagnac or American brandy)
  • .5 oz Orgeat syrup
  • 1-2x dash Angostura bitters

Stir; strain over rocks; lemon twist.

Drink and enjoy! I love this cocktail because it highlights the best attributes my favorite spirit, brandy. It's slightly sweet, but not too unctuous, fruity, spicy, nutty. What more could you ask for??? Great year-round as well!

What's your favorite simple cocktail?

Cheers!

Awesome post, thanks for it! My favorite, if you couldn't guess by looking at my post, is the recently rediscovered Moscow Mule!

INGREDIENTS

  1. Juice of one lime
  2. 3 Ounce Russian Standard Vodka
  3. 6 Ounce cold ginger beer (not to be confused with ginger ale)
  4. 3 Drops Angostura bitters
  5. Twist of lime, for garnish

Preparation:

  1. In a Collins glass — or a copper mug, if you own one — squeeze the juice of one lime and fill with crushed ice.

  2. Pour the vodka and stir. Fill the glass with cold ginger beer. As for the bitters, according to César Raúl Córdova Rogerone— a Moscow Mule connoisseur — it works better if the bitters sort of float on the surface and make their way slowly to the bottom of the glass, leaving a lovely hint of smoke on the way down. You won’t get this visual effect if you use a copper mug, of course, but the bitters are still worth every drop.

  3. Garnish with a twist of lime.

Source: This particular prep and recipe shamelessly stolen from here

Moscow Mules are great! And a wonderful way to get people more interested in cocktails beyond vodka/soda. Ever tried a gin-gin mule?

  • 2 oz gin
  • .5 oz lime
  • .5 oz mint syrup
  • 5 mint leaves
  • Ginger beer

 

  1. Softly muddle the mint with lime and syrup
  2. Short shake mint, lime, syrup, and gin
  3. Pour over ice in collins (double-strained to avoid mint shards)
  4. Top with ginger beer
  5. Garnish with mint sprig (or lime wheel if you don't want to bother with mint)

It's a wonderful summer variation on the Moscow Mule, and I usually offer it as a softball introductory gin cocktail as well.

Cheers!
